name: Dzongkha
notes: Dzongkha (རྫོང་ཁ), national language of Bhutan, written in the Tibetan script (Uchen/Joyi), an abugida. RESEARCH-tier SKELETON: this spec is the base-letter → phoneme table only (consonant carries inherent /a/ unless a vowel sign is present), exactly the same simplification the sibling Tibetan-script spec `bo` (Classical/Lhasa Tibetan) uses — it does NOT resolve the prefix/superscript/root/subscript/suffix consonant STACKS that Dzongkha spelling actually encodes (van Driem 1998, 'Dzongkha', ch. 2-3): real Dzongkha words collapse a written cluster to a single onset plus a TONE that this base-letter table cannot derive (e.ke.g. སྤྲོད spelled with a superscript ⟨ས⟩, base ⟨པ⟩ and subscript ⟨ར⟩ surfaces as [ʈøː˥], not a letter-by-letter reading). Resolving the stack system is the documented gap in the upstream stub note and remains a known engine/spec limitation, listed here rather than masked. WikiPron gold (`dzo_tibt_broad.tsv`, 243 rows) is registered and scored honestly against this base-letter table; the resulting PER reflects that known gap, not an inherent limit of the writing system, and the spec stays at `research` (not `production`) tier as a result — see docs/quality_tiers.md (research tier has no PER ceiling, only a benchmark-recorded requirement). Voicing: ག/ད/བ/ཛ are the 'voiced' letters, phonetically PLAIN (unaspirated) in Standard Dzongkha per van Driem, contrasting with the plain-vs-aspirated pairs ཀ/ཁ, ཏ/ཐ, པ/ཕ, ཙ/ཚ — the historical voicing distinction of Classical Tibetan corresponds to a TONE distinction in Dzongkha, not a voicing distinction, matching the same voiced-to-tone shift already documented for `bo`. STRESS/TONE EXEMPTION: Dzongkha is tonal, not stress-accented; no `stress` block is declared, and tone is not derivable from the base-letter table alone (see the stack-resolution gap above), so it is not asserted here either.
